definitions.explanation: A gathering of vendors selling goods, typically held periodically at a specific location. Can be a traditional open-air market or a special event.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}{市|いち}で{野菜|やさい}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought vegetables at the morning market.

examples.japanese: {毎月|まいつき}{第|だい}{一|いち}{日曜日|にちようび}に{蚤|のみ}の{市|いち}が{開|ひら}かれる。
examples.english: A flea market is held on the first Sunday of every month.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}の{魚|さかな}{市|いち}は{大|おお}にぎわいだ。
examples.english: The year-end fish market is very crowded.

notes:
{市|いち} refers to a traditional market or fair, distinct from {市|し} which means "city."

COMMON TYPES OF MARKETS:
- {朝|あさ}{市|いち}: morning market
- {夕|ゆう}{市|いち}: evening market
- {蚤|のみ}の{市|いち}: flea market
- {魚|さかな}{市|いち}: fish market
- {骨董|こっとう}{市|いち}: antique market
- {手作|てづく}り{市|いち}: handcraft market
- クリスマス{市|いち} / クリスマスマーケット: Christmas market

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マーケット: market (loanword)
- {市場|いちば}: marketplace, market
- {市場|しじょう}: market (economic sense)

USAGE:
Be careful not to confuse {市|いち} (market) with {市|し} (city).
